name: Jacqueline Glass
life: “I still remember returning a paragraph with just its finest line intact.” On Sunday, near the approach to Seabright Court, Jacqueline likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I edited the manuscript so heavily I was beginning to hear my own voice. I'm pleased it's hers again.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a black overshirt with pearl buttons and one cuff folded back twice. Jacqueline has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, with brown hair pinned away from the temples. Jacqueline looks toward the door whenever a name is called during a conversation.
personality: Jacqueline keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Jacqueline wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To return the pages in the author's own voice.
family: Emery Colón is Jacqueline’s half-sibling. Jacqueline is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Emery calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *One paid trial*, Emery says, “I caught a bus across town for the cheap day-old bread.”
connections: Hamish Yeo. One supporter paid to keep the lights on while another kept the writer's own voice audible.

reactions.situation: A reader asks for a copy with the page still blank
reactions.response: Jacqueline keeps a clean, blank copy aside for the reader to dedicate.

reactions.situation: A customer is short at the till while a queue forms
reactions.response: Jacqueline keeps the customer's place while they check the amount and gets the impatient people talking about something else.

reactions.situation: When somebody asks who said it first
reactions.response: Jacqueline offers to introduce them to the person willing to put a name to it.
